nodes.description: Disturbed chondrocyte differentiation in the vertebral and epiphyseal growth plates produces the characteristic platyspondyly and epiphyseal dysplasia. The mechanistic detail linking TRPV4 channel dysfunction to the specific Maroteaux-type radiographic pattern — as opposed to the Kozlowski or metatropic patterns — has not been established.

The five autosomal dominant skeletal dysplasias are (from mildest to most severe) familial digital arthropathy with brachydactyly, brachyolmia, spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (Kozlowski type), spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (Maroteaux type), and metatropic dysplasia.

All TRPV4-related skeletal dysplasias are characterized by brachydactyly; the four most severe forms have short stature that varies from mild to severe with progressive spinal deformity and involvement of the long bones and pelvis.

nodes.description: Disproportionate short stature with a short trunk, not evident at birth and becoming apparent in childhood. Vertebral flattening supplies the trunk component; GeneReviews records long-bone involvement in the four more severe TRPV4 skeletal dysplasias, so the vertebrae are not the sole contributor.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants in TRPV4 alter the gating of a calcium-permeable mechanosensitive cation channel in chondrocytes. Several of the variants found in SEDM patients are the same substitutions reported in metatropic dysplasia, so the variant alone does not determine which phenotype in the TRPV4 family results.

evidence.reference_title: Spondylo-epiphyseal dysplasia, Maroteaux type (pseudo-Morquio syndrome type 2), and parastremmatic dysplasia are caused by TRPV4 mutations.
evidence.snippet: We tested the hypothesis that a further condition, Spondylo-epiphyseal dysplasia (SED), Maroteaux type (MIM 184095; also known as pseudo-Morquio syndrome type 2), could be caused by TRPV4 mutations.

evidence.snippet: We conclude that SED Maroteaux type and parastremmatic dysplasia are part of the TRPV4 dysplasia family and that TRPV4 mutations show considerable variability in phenotypic expression resulting in distinct clinical-radiographic phenotypes.

nodes.description: Generalized platyspondyly without the anterior tongue-like vertebral deformity of Morquio syndrome. A tissue-level structural outcome of the disordered growth plate, kept separate from the organism-level stature deficit it contributes to.

evidence.snippet: Platyspondylysis is present but there are no anterior tongue-like deformities of the vertebral bodies.
